proposals.citation: CDIAL[6328];varkey-vunnamatla2018bareli[Appendix C.3, printed p. 118, item 117, Parya Bhilali-Bhorwada]
proposals.evidence: CDIAL dina supplies regional din “day, daytime”. The same surveyed language independently attests dīn “day” (f_eoeugdovfpnoy), supporting the local day/sun polysemy rather than choosing a remote sun root by sound alone. The source’s sun gloss, vowel length and dental/retroflex spelling are retained. This identifies the day-word family and leaves possible intra-Indo-Aryan transmission open.
